test_title: PYST 31: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What was the main objective of India’s First Five Year Plan (1951–56)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan of India (1951–56) focused primarily on **Agricultural development**. It emphasized increasing food production to address the issue of food scarcity and laid the foundation for agricultural modernization.
 
• The Plan was launched under the leadership of **Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first Prime Minister of India, and was based on the **Harrod-Domar model**, which prioritized investment in the agricultural sector.
 
• Agriculture contributed significantly to the Indian economy at that time, accounting for a majority of the GDP and employing the largest portion of the population. Hence, its development was a critical need.
 
• Key initiatives under the First Five-Year Plan included the establishment of major irrigation projects like the **Bhakra-Nangal Dam**, **DVC (Damodar Valley Corporation)**, and **Hirakud Dam** to improve water supply for agriculture.
 
• The Plan achieved success with a growth rate of **3.6%**, surpassing the target of 2.1%, largely due to favorable monsoons and the focus on agricultural productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heavy Industrialization:**

 
 
• Although industrialization was a part of subsequent Five-Year Plans, the First Plan did not focus heavily on it. Industrial development gained prominence during the **Second Five-Year Plan**, which emphasized the growth of the public sector and heavy industries under the leadership of **Dr. P.C. Mahalanobis**.
 
• Examples of industries promoted later include steel plants in **Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela**.
 
 
 
• **Privatization of PSUs:**
 
 
• Privatization of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) was not a focus during the First Five-Year Plan. In fact, the Plan emphasized the role of the **public sector** in national development.
 
• Privatization gained momentum in India much later, during the **1990s**, as part of economic reforms under the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** policy.
 
 
 
• **Growth of IT Services:**
 
 
• The development of Information Technology (IT) services was not a focus in the First Five-Year Plan. IT services began developing much later in India, particularly in the **1980s and 1990s**, with cities like **Bengaluru** emerging as IT hubs.
 
• Major initiatives in IT were introduced as part of **economic liberalization**, which encouraged private sector involvement and investment in technology.
 
 
 
• **First Five-Year Plan Highlights:**
 
 
• Objective: To address challenges like food shortages, poverty, and inflation.
 
• Sector Allocation: **44.6%** of the total budget was allocated to agriculture and irrigation.
 
• Achievements: Successful implementation of irrigation projects and agricultural modernization.
 
• Outcome: Laid the foundation for future economic and social development in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• India adopted the concept of Five-Year Plans from the **Soviet Union**, aiming for systematic economic development.
 
• These plans were developed and monitored by the **Planning Commission**, which was established in **1950** by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• The First Plan prioritized agriculture as India was primarily an agrarian economy with food shortages.
 
• Subsequent plans shifted focus to industrialization, infrastructure, and social development.
 
 
 
• **Bhakra-Nangal Dam:**
 
 
• One of the largest dam projects undertaken during the First Five-Year Plan.
 
• Located on the **Sutlej River**, it provides irrigation, hydropower, and flood control in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• Established in **1948**, DVC aimed to control floods, provide irrigation, and generate hydropower in the Damodar River basin.
 
• It served as a model for integrated resource management during the First Plan.
